s: tare (the empty weight of a container)
Tara.et: Borrowed from Italian tara, from Arabic طَرْح (ṭarḥ, “subtraction”).

Tarnkappe.et:
From Middle High German tarnkappe. The first element is likely related to Proto-West Germanic *darnī (“secret, hidden”) and the second element is from Kappe.
By surface analysis, tarnen + Kappe.

tarnen.et: Early 20th century, a borrowing (inspired by older Tarnkappe) from Middle High German tarnen, from Old High German *tarnōn, from Proto-West Germanic *darnōn. Cognate with English darn.

s: tarantula (Lycosa tarantula, kind of wolf spider of southern Europe)
certain other large species of wolf spider, chiefly of the genera Alopecosa, Hogna, Lycosa
the disused wolf spider genus Tarentula
a New World tarantula (spider of the family Theraphosidae)

Tarif.et: From Arabic تَعَارِيف (taʕārīf, “fees to be paid”).

Tartsche.et: From Middle High German tartsche, from Old French targe, from Old Norse targa, from Proto-Germanic *targǭ. Compare cognate Old High German zarga, whence modern Zarge (“frame”), Old English targe, whereas Middle Low German tartze, tartzge and Middle Dutch tarch…

s: A game played with tarot cards.
according to the agreed union rate
Taranto (a city and province of Italy)
a municipality of Upper Austria, Austria

Tartaros.et: Borrowed from Ancient Greek Τάρταρος (Tártaros), possibly through Latin Tartaros.

Tarte.et: Fairly recent borrowing from French tarte.

t: „Wo ist denn Tara?“ – „Die duscht.“
"Where's Tara?" "She's taking a shower."
l: Frauen, die den Mut haben, fraulich zu sein, mütterlich zu sein wie Tara, die Große Mutter, die Göttin aller wunderbaren Energien.
Weiter als Mihambo sprang in dieser Hallensaison nur die Amerikanerin Tara Davis-Woodhall, die am Wochenende bei den US-Meisterschaften 7,18 Meter schaffte.

t: Der Kuchen war als voller Aschenbecher getarnt.
The cake was disguised as a full ashtray.
Tom versuchte sich zu tarnen.
Tom tried to camouflage himself.

l: Vielleicht war diese eine Sache zu offensichtlich, zu schlecht getarnt, zu plump.

t: Wenn ich Toki Pona studiere, erinnere ich mich, dass Tarzan sagte: "Ich Tarzan, du Jane."

t: Er war wie von der Tarantel gestochen.
